# MEMORANDUM

**To:** [Supervising Partner]
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** October 18, 2026
**Re:** Harrowgate Bottling Co. / Veltmar Glassworks, Inc.: Risk review of current supply contract documents

---

## I. Summary

We reviewed four documents:

- the Supply Agreement effective March 1, 2024 (the "**SA**");
- the non-binding Term Sheet dated January 22, 2024;
- Amendment No. 1 dated September 21, 2026 (the "**Amendment**"); and
- the Quality and Specifications Agreement (the "**QA**").

All are governed by Delaware law (SA § 15.5; Amendment § 6.1; QA § 11.5).

Before turning to the issues, one structural point governs much of the analysis. Under **SA § 15.2 (Order of Precedence)**, documents control in this order: written amendments, then the Supply Agreement, then the Quality Agreement. Amendment § 5.2 expressly designates itself a "written amendment" for purposes of §§ 15.2 and 15.3. **Where the Amendment conflicts with the SA, the Amendment controls.** The Term Sheet does not appear in the order of precedence at all. SA § 15.1 (Entire Agreement) expressly supersedes prior "term sheets."

There are five material issues, listed in suggested order of client discussion:

| # | Issue | Location | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Expired 30-day window to object to 14% price increase | Amendment, Recital C; SA § 5.4 | High / time-critical |
| 2 | Recall and product-liability exposure now subject to the six-month cap | Amendment § 2; SA §§ 11.1–11.2 | High |
| 3 | Automatic five-year renewals with a narrow 30-day opt-out window | SA § 2.2 | High / time-critical |
| 4 | Exclusivity far broader than the agreed deal | SA § 3.1 vs. Term Sheet § 2 | High |
| 5 | Veltmar may assign freely, including to a competitor | Amendment § 4 (new SA § 14.4) | Medium–High |

The QA raised no independent issues (see Part III). Part IV lists open questions for the client.

---

## II. Issues

### Issue 1: The window to object to the 14% price increase has closed

**Location:** Amendment No. 1, Recital C; Supply Agreement §§ 5.3–5.4.

**What the documents say.**

- **SA § 5.4** allows Harrowgate to object to a Price Adjustment Notice "within 30 days after Customer's receipt." Any adjustment not objected to in time "is deemed accepted by Customer and takes effect on the date stated in the Price Adjustment Notice."
- **Amendment Recital C** records three things:
  - Veltmar's notice (dated July 30, 2026) of a **14%** increase effective October 2, 2026, "was received by Customer on August 3, 2026";
  - "[n]o objection … has been delivered by Customer"; and
  - the notice "remains subject to Section 5.4."

**Why it matters.**

- Thirty days after August 3, 2026 is **September 2, 2026**. The objection window therefore closed **19 days before the Amendment's own date of September 21, 2026**.
- Nothing in the Amendment extends the deadline, reopens it or waives it. Amendment § 5.3 confirms that nothing in it waives any right "except as expressly set out."
- The statement that the notice "remains subject to Section 5.4" does not help Harrowgate. Section 5.4 itself supplies the deemed-acceptance consequence. Harrowgate has also now signed (or will sign) a recital acknowledging the receipt date and the absence of any objection.
- **On the face of the documents, the 14% increase is deemed accepted.** It took effect on October 2, 2026 and is already in force.
- Harrowgate cannot now serve a timely § 5.4 objection. Any attempt to do so should not be treated as preserving rights.
- Under SA § 2.2, the increased pricing carries into any Renewal Term (see Issue 3).

**Possible arguments to investigate.** These are not to be relied on without client facts.

1. **Notice defects under § 5.3.** A notice qualifies as a "Price Adjustment Notice" only if it includes "reasonable supporting detail of the cost changes." If the July 30 notice lacked that detail, Harrowgate may argue it was never a valid notice and the objection clock never started.
2. **Frequency limit.** Adjustments are limited to once per 12-month period. We should confirm there was no other adjustment within the preceding 12 months.
3. **Method of delivery.** We should check whether the notice was delivered by a method permitted by § 15.4. The Amendment's statement that it was "received" on August 3 likely undercuts this argument.

**Recommended fix.**

- Seek an express written extension or waiver from Veltmar. This could be done as part of a further amendment or by revising the Amendment if it has not yet been executed (see Part IV).
- Leverage could come from Harrowgate's concessions in the Amendment, which appear to have been given for no evident consideration.

**Proposed language** (new Amendment section):

> "**Price Adjustment Notice of July 30, 2026.** Notwithstanding Section 5.4 of the Agreement or Recital C of this Amendment, the period within which Customer may object to Supplier's Price Adjustment Notice dated July 30, 2026 is extended to, and shall expire on, [date at least 30 days after signing]. Any objection delivered by Customer on or before that date shall be deemed timely under Section 5.4. Pending resolution under Section 5.4, the prices in Exhibit B in effect immediately before October 2, 2026 shall apply, and Supplier shall credit Customer for any amounts invoiced at the adjusted prices. Customer's failure to object before the Amendment Date shall not constitute acceptance of the adjustment."

Recital C should also be revised to delete the acknowledgment that no objection was delivered, or to make it expressly subject to this extension.

---

### Issue 2: Amendment No. 1 removes recall costs and product-liability indemnities from the liability-cap carve-outs

**Location:** Amendment No. 1 § 2 (replacing SA § 11.2); SA §§ 9.1, 10.2, 11.1, 11.3.

**What the documents say.**

- **SA § 11.1** caps each Party's total liability at **"the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose."**
- **Original SA § 11.2** excluded four categories from the cap and from the § 11.3 consequential-damages bar:
  - (a) all of Supplier's § 9.1 indemnities;
  - (b) Recall costs under § 10;
  - (c) confidentiality breaches; and
  - (d) gross negligence, fraud or willful misconduct.
- This matched Term Sheet § 7.2.
- **Amendment § 2.1** replaces § 11.2 with three exclusions:
  - (a) Supplier's § 9.1 indemnities, "which are excluded **solely to third-party intellectual property claims under Section 9.1(c)**";
  - (b) confidentiality breaches; and
  - (c) gross negligence, fraud or willful misconduct.
- **The Recall carve-out is deleted entirely.** The change applies to claims arising on or after September 21, 2026 (Amendment § 2.2).
- Under § 15.2, the Amendment controls.

**Why it matters.**

- Harrowgate's largest realistic exposures as a beverage bottler are a contaminated or defective bottle recall (glass inclusions, cracked finishes and similar defects) and resulting consumer injury claims. Both are now capped at six months of fees. They include:
  - **Recall costs under § 10.2**: retrieval, destruction, lost beverage contents, replacement product and customer credits.
  - **Product-defect and personal-injury indemnities under § 9.1(a), (b) and (d).**
- A single recall could readily exceed six months of container spend.
- Because these items are no longer excluded from § 11.3, Veltmar can also argue that significant recall components are barred entirely as "consequential" damages or "lost profits." Examples include lost beverage contents, customer credits and downstream losses.
- Recitals present the Amendment as a "clarification." Substantively, it reallocates the core product risk to Harrowgate.
- **Drafting point.** The phrase "excluded solely to third-party intellectual property claims" is ungrammatical. Veltmar will read it as limiting the indemnity carve-out to § 9.1(c). We should not rely on the defect to argue a broader reading.
- **Timing point.** Disputes may arise over when a "claim arose" for products delivered before the Amendment Date but discovered later.

**Recommended fix.** Restore the original § 11.2. As a fallback, at minimum restore the Recall and § 9.1(a), (b) and (d) carve-outs, or set a separate super-cap tied to the $10,000,000 insurance limit in § 14.1. In the interim, confirm the status of Veltmar's product recall and product liability insurance and Harrowgate's additional-insured status, because insurance may be the practical source of recovery.

**Proposed language:**

> "Section 11.2 of the Agreement (as amended by Amendment No. 1) is deleted and replaced with the following:
> '11.2 **Exclusions.** The limitation in Section 11.1 and the exclusion in Section 11.3 do not apply to (a) Supplier's indemnity obligations under Section 9.1 (including Sections 9.1(a) through (d)); (b) Recall costs under Section 10; (c) either Party's breach of Section 12; or (d) a Party's gross negligence, fraud or willful misconduct.'
> This Section 11.2 applies to all claims, whenever arising, including claims relating to Products delivered before the Amendment Date."

---

### Issue 3: Automatic five-year renewals with a narrow 30-day opt-out window

**Location:** Supply Agreement § 2.2.

**What the document says.**

- The Initial Term is three years from March 1, 2024 (§ 2.1).
- Under § 2.2, the Agreement "shall automatically renew for **successive five-year Renewal Terms**." Renewal is avoided only if notice of non-renewal is given "**not more than 270 days and not less than 240 days**" before expiry.
- All terms, "including Sections 3 and 5" (exclusivity and price adjustments), continue during each Renewal Term.
- The Term Sheet (§ 3.2) left renewal mechanics to be negotiated. Nothing in it contemplated five-year evergreen terms.

**Why it matters.**

- The opt-out right is effectively a **30-day window**. Notice given one day early or one day late is ineffective, and Harrowgate is then locked in for **five more years**. That lock-in would come with broad exclusivity (Issue 4), the deemed-accepted 14% increase (Issue 1), the reduced liability carve-outs (Issue 2) and Veltmar's free assignment right (Issue 5).
- **Time-critical point.** The Initial Term expires on or about March 1, 2027. Counting back:
  - 270 days before is about **June 4, 2026**;
  - 240 days before is about **July 4, 2026**.
- **On our calculation, the non-renewal window for the Initial Term has already closed.** Unless Harrowgate served compliant notice under § 15.4 between roughly June 4 and July 4, 2026, the Agreement will renew on or about March 1, 2027, through about March 1, 2032.
- The exact expiry date (February 28 or March 1, 2027) may shift the window by a day. That ambiguity is itself a reason to fix the clause.
- If renewal occurs, the next window would open about June 4, 2031 and close about July 4, 2031.
- Harrowgate's only other exit routes are termination for uncured material breach or insolvency (§§ 13.1–13.2).

**Recommended fix.**

1. Confirm immediately with the client whether any non-renewal notice was served in June–July 2026 (see Part IV).
2. Calendar the next window now, with multiple reminders.
3. Negotiate the following changes:
   - one-year (or at most two-year) renewal terms;
   - a broad notice window (any time up to 90 days before expiry);
   - a termination-for-convenience right during any Renewal Term; and
   - if the Initial Term window has closed, an express agreement that the March 2027 renewal will not be triggered, or will be for a short term only.

**Proposed language** (replacement § 2.2):

> "2.2 **Renewal.** At the end of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one-year Renewal Terms (each, a "**Renewal Term**") unless either Party gives the other written notice of non-renewal at any time not less than ninety (90) days before the expiration of the Initial Term or the then-current Renewal Term. In addition, during any Renewal Term, Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience on one hundred eighty (180) days' written notice to Supplier without liability, other than payment for Products delivered and for the firm portion of Customer's forecast. Notwithstanding any prior failure to give notice, the Parties agree that the Initial Term shall expire on [date] [and that any Renewal Term commencing on or about March 1, 2027 shall be a one-year Renewal Term]."

---

### Issue 4: Exclusivity is far broader than the deal recorded in the term sheet

**Location:** Supply Agreement § 3.1; compare Term Sheet § 2. See also SA §§ 15.1, 15.2 and 15.7, and Exhibit A.

**What the documents say.**

- **SA § 3.1** makes Veltmar Harrowgate's exclusive source of "**all glass and PET containers for any beverage product** manufactured, filled, bottled or packaged by or for Customer or its Affiliates, **worldwide**." Harrowgate must also cause its Affiliates not to buy from third parties.
- **Term Sheet § 2.1** recorded the agreed scope as "**amber glass bottles for Customer's beer brands at its U.S. and Canadian facilities**."
- **Term Sheet § 2.2** expressly preserved Harrowgate's freedom to source "containers for non-beer products, containers made from materials other than amber glass, and containers for facilities outside the United States and Canada."

**Why it matters.**

- **The executed text controls, not the Term Sheet.** The Term Sheet is expressly non-binding except for §§ 10–11. SA § 15.1 supersedes prior "term sheets," and the Term Sheet has no place in the § 15.2 order of precedence. Harrowgate is bound by the broader § 3.1 scope.
- Reformation for mutual mistake, or a fraud-type theory based on the drafting history, would require strong evidence under Delaware law. These should be treated as fallbacks, not as a basis for current planning.
- As drafted, § 3.1 captures several categories outside the agreed deal:
  - non-beer lines (water, soft drinks, ready-to-drink products);
  - **all PET packaging**;
  - flint or green glass; and
  - every current or future facility, and every Affiliate's facility, outside the U.S. and Canada.
- Any third-party purchases in these categories are a breach of § 3.1 and could support termination or damages claims by Veltmar.
- **Supply gap.** Exhibit A lists only three amber beer bottles, and Veltmar has no obligation to supply PET or other containers. Harrowgate may therefore be barred from buying containers that Veltmar does not make or will not supply. The only relief is force majeure (§ 15.7), which requires a 30-day-plus event beyond Veltmar's control.
- Exclusivity carries into each five-year Renewal Term (§ 2.2).

**Recommended fix.**

- Amend § 3.1 to restore the Term Sheet scope.
- Add a carve-out for products Veltmar cannot or does not supply on competitive terms.
- Separately, confirm whether Harrowgate or its Affiliates currently buy any glass or PET containers from third parties. Such purchases may already be breaches (see Part IV).

**Proposed language** (replacement § 3.1):

> "3.1 **Exclusive Purchase.** During the Term, Customer shall purchase from Supplier, and Supplier shall be Customer's exclusive source of, amber glass bottles of the types listed in Exhibit A for Customer's beer brands filled at Customer's facilities located in the United States and Canada (the "**Exclusive Products**"). Customer and its Affiliates remain free to purchase from any third party all other containers, including containers for non-beer products, containers made of any material other than amber glass (including PET), and containers for facilities outside the United States and Canada. Customer may also purchase Exclusive Products from third parties, without breach of this Section 3.1, to the extent Supplier rejects, fails to accept within the period in Section 4.1, or fails to deliver on time any Purchase Order for them."

---

### Issue 5: Veltmar may now assign without consent, including to a competitor, while Harrowgate remains bound

**Location:** Amendment No. 1 § 4 (new SA § 14.4); SA § 14.3.

**What the documents say.**

- **SA § 14.3** (consistent with Term Sheet § 8.1) bars either Party from assigning without the other's prior written consent.
- **New § 14.4**, added "[n]otwithstanding Section 14.3," allows Supplier to assign the Agreement "in whole or in part," or any rights or obligations under it, "**without the consent of Customer**" to:
  - (a) any Affiliate; or
  - (b) any successor by merger, consolidation, change of control or sale of all or substantially all of the relevant business or assets.
- Notice is required only **within 30 days after** the assignment takes effect.
- Under § 15.2, the Amendment overrides § 14.3 as to Veltmar.

**Why it matters.**

- **The restriction is now one-sided.** Harrowgate still needs Veltmar's consent for any assignment, including in its own M&A transactions. Veltmar needs none.
- **There is no competitor exclusion.** Veltmar could be acquired by, or assign to, a Harrowgate competitor, for example a vertically integrated brewer or bottler. That party would then:
  - hold an exclusive worldwide supply right over Harrowgate (Issue 4);
  - receive Harrowgate's monthly 12-month forecasts by product and location (§ 3.2);
  - receive pricing and other Confidential Information; and
  - control the supply of Harrowgate's packaging.
- **There is no creditworthiness, capability or quality condition.** An Affiliate assignee could be a thinly capitalized shell. That matters more now that recall and product-liability recovery is capped (Issue 2).
- **Partial assignment** ("in part") could split supply, warranty, indemnity and recall obligations across different entities. This would complicate enforcement.
- Harrowgate has no termination right on a change of control and receives notice only after the fact.

**Recommended fix.**

- Delete § 14.4, or narrow it.
- Make any permitted assignment conditional on the following:
  - no assignment to a Competitor;
  - an assignee of equal or better creditworthiness that assumes all obligations in writing;
  - no partial assignment;
  - Veltmar's continued guarantee; and
  - advance notice, with a Harrowgate termination right on any change of control.
- Alternatively, make the carve-out mutual.

**Proposed language** (replacement § 14.4):

> "14.4 **Permitted Assignment.** Notwithstanding Section 14.3, either Party may assign this Agreement in whole, but not in part, without the other Party's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor by merger, consolidation, change of control or sale of all or substantially all of the business or assets to which this Agreement relates, provided that: (a) the assigning Party gives the other Party at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice; (b) the assignee assumes in writing all of the assigning Party's obligations under this Agreement; (c) the assignee has creditworthiness, insurance and manufacturing capability reasonably equivalent to or better than those of the assigning Party; and (d) in the case of an assignment by Supplier, the assigning Party remains jointly and severally liable for the assignee's obligations. Supplier shall not assign this Agreement, and no change of control of Supplier shall occur, in favor of any person that produces, bottles or distributes beverage products in competition with Customer or its Affiliates (a "**Competitor**") without Customer's prior written consent. If a change of control of Supplier occurs, Customer may terminate this Agreement on ninety (90) days' written notice without liability. Any assignment in violation of this Section 14.4 is void."

---

## III. Quality and Specifications Agreement: no independent issues

We reviewed the QA in full. It is consistent with the SA and does not raise material independent risk for Harrowgate. Specifically:

- It defers to the SA order of precedence (QA § 1.3).
- It tracks the three amber beer bottles in Exhibit A (Schedule 1).
- It routes Recalls to SA § 10 (QA § 9.2).
- It contains buyer-favorable quality controls: zero-tolerance AQL for Critical Defects, 24-hour Critical Defect notice, 90-day change-control notice, and audit rights.

Two observations:

1. The QA's Recall cooperation provisions are of limited value if recall costs remain capped under the Amendment (Issue 2).
2. The QA covers only amber glass. This underscores the mismatch between the operational scope of the relationship and the worldwide glass-and-PET exclusivity in SA § 3.1 (Issue 4).

---

## IV. Open questions for the client

We need the following information to complete the analysis. We have not made assumptions on these points.

1. **Execution of the Amendment.** The copy in the folder has blank signature blocks. Has Amendment No. 1 been signed by both parties? If not, Issues 1, 2 and 5 can be addressed by revising it before signature, and Harrowgate should not sign in its current form.
2. **Non-renewal notice.** Did Harrowgate serve written notice of non-renewal under SA § 15.4 between about June 4 and July 4, 2026? If not, the Agreement appears set to renew on or about March 1, 2027 for five years.
3. **Price Adjustment Notice.** Please provide a copy of the July 30, 2026 notice, with evidence of how and when it was delivered. We also need to know whether any other price adjustment occurred in the preceding 12 months, and whether Harrowgate has already paid invoices at the increased prices.
4. **Current sourcing.** Do Harrowgate or its Affiliates buy any glass or PET containers from third parties, for non-beer lines, PET packaging or facilities outside the U.S. and Canada? Are any such facilities or lines planned?
5. **Negotiation history.** Does the client have drafts or correspondence showing how § 3.1 moved from the Term Sheet scope to the executed text? This is relevant to any reformation fallback and to negotiating leverage.
6. **Consideration and context for the Amendment.** What, if anything, did Harrowgate receive in exchange for the Amendment's concessions? This bears on leverage for a further amendment.
7. **Insurance.** Has Harrowgate received current certificates confirming Veltmar's $10,000,000 product liability and product recall coverage and Harrowgate's additional-insured status (SA § 14.1)?
8. **Veltmar ownership.** Is the client aware of any pending sale, merger or change of control of Veltmar, or of any affiliation between Veltmar and a Harrowgate competitor?

---

## V. Recommended next steps

1. **Immediately:** confirm answers to Questions 1–3, which are time-sensitive. If the Amendment is unsigned, hold signature.
2. **Prepare a proposed Amendment No. 2** (or a revised Amendment No. 1) incorporating:
   - the price-objection extension (Issue 1);
   - the restored § 11.2 (Issue 2);
   - the revised § 2.2 (Issue 3);
   - the narrowed § 3.1 (Issue 4); and
   - the revised § 14.4 (Issue 5).
3. **Calendar** all non-renewal windows, with reminders at 300, 280 and 260 days before each expiry date.
4. **Advise the client** to avoid third-party container purchases that could breach § 3.1 until scope is renegotiated.

I am happy to walk through any of these items before the client call.

  - **(b) Negotiated fix.** More realistically, negotiate an express extension or waiver in a further amendment, ideally as part of a package with the other items in this memo.

**Proposed language (Amendment No. 2):**

> "**Price Adjustment Notice of July 30, 2026.** Notwithstanding Section 5.4 of the Agreement or any prior expiration of the objection period stated in it, the Parties agree that (a) the Price Adjustment Notice dated July 30, 2026 is not deemed accepted by Customer; (b) Customer may deliver a written objection to that Price Adjustment Notice at any time within thirty (30) days after the date of this Amendment, and any such objection shall be treated as timely under Section 5.4; and (c) pending completion of the negotiation and dispute resolution process in Section 5.4, the prices in Exhibit B in effect immediately before October 2, 2026 shall apply, and Supplier shall credit Customer for any amounts invoiced in excess of those prices for Products delivered on or after October 2, 2026."

### Item 3: Overbroad Exclusivity Compared with the Negotiated Deal

**Location:** Supply Agreement, Section 3.1, compared with Term Sheet, Section 2. Also relevant: SA Sections 15.1 and 15.2.

**What it says:**

- SA Section 3.1 requires Harrowgate to buy from Veltmar, as its exclusive source, "**all glass and PET containers** for any beverage product manufactured, filled, bottled or packaged by or for Customer or its Affiliates, **worldwide**."
- It also prohibits Harrowgate and its Affiliates from buying any such containers from third parties.
- By contrast, Term Sheet Section 2.1 records the agreed exclusivity as "**amber glass bottles** for Customer's **beer brands** at its **U.S. and Canadian facilities**."
- Term Sheet Section 2.2 expressly preserves Harrowgate's freedom to source non-beer containers, non-amber-glass containers and containers for non-U.S./Canada facilities.

**Why it matters for Harrowgate:**

- **The executed text is much wider than the agreed deal.** It sweeps in:
  - non-beer lines (soft drinks, water, cider, spirits, RTDs);
  - all PET packaging;
  - flint and green glass;
  - every current and future facility worldwide; and
  - Affiliates' purchasing.
- **Harrowgate is bound by the broader executed text.**
  - The Term Sheet is expressly non-binding on this point.
  - It is superseded by the entire-agreement clause (SA Section 15.1, which specifically names "term sheets").
  - It has no place in the Section 15.2 order of precedence.
  - The Term Sheet is helpful evidence of the parties' intent for a reformation or mutual-mistake argument, or as negotiating leverage. However, I would not advise the client that the narrower scope governs. Reformation under Delaware law requires clear and convincing evidence and is uncertain.
- **The mismatch creates a practical trap.**
  - Exhibit A lists only three amber beer bottles. Veltmar has no stated obligation to supply PET, non-amber glass or containers for other beverages. Section 3.3 capacity and Section 4.1 order acceptance are tied to "Products."
  - Harrowgate may therefore be prohibited from buying certain containers elsewhere even though Veltmar has no obligation to supply them.
  - The only built-in relief is the 30-day force majeure carve-out in Section 15.7.
- **Possible existing breach.** If Harrowgate or its Affiliates currently buy PET or other containers from third parties, they may already be in breach of Section 3.1. That would expose them to a Section 13.1 termination notice or damages claim.
- **The exposure is extended.** It continues through any Renewal Term (Item 1) and would pass to any assignee of Veltmar (Item 4).

**Information needed from the client:**

1. A list of all containers (material, color, beverage line, facility) that Harrowgate and its Affiliates currently buy from suppliers other than Veltmar, and since when.
2. Whether Harrowgate has any planned non-U.S./Canada facilities or new beverage lines.
3. Whether Veltmar has ever asserted the broader scope, or whether the parties' course of dealing has been limited to amber beer bottles.
4. Who negotiated the definitive SA, and whether any drafts or correspondence explain the change from the Term Sheet scope. This bears on any reformation argument.

**Recommended fix:**

1. Negotiate a replacement Section 3.1 that restores the Term Sheet scope.
2. Ask Veltmar to confirm in writing that it will not assert breach for past third-party purchases outside that scope.
3. If any existing third-party purchasing is identified, address it in the same amendment through an express release.

**Proposed language (replacement Section 3.1):**

> "3.1 **Exclusive Purchase.** During the Term, Customer shall purchase from Supplier, and Supplier shall be Customer's exclusive source of, amber glass bottles of the types listed in Exhibit A for Customer's beer brands filled at Customer's facilities located in the United States and Canada (the "**Exclusive Products**"). Nothing in this Agreement restricts Customer or its Affiliates from purchasing from any third party (a) containers for non-beer products; (b) containers made of any material other than amber glass, including PET and flint or green glass; (c) containers for use at any facility outside the United States and Canada; or (d) any Exclusive Products that Supplier is unable or fails to supply in accordance with an accepted Purchase Order or Section 3.3."

> "**Release.** Supplier waives and releases any claim that any purchase by Customer or its Affiliates before the date of this Amendment of containers outside the scope of Section 3.1 (as amended) breached Section 3.1 of the Agreement."

### Item 4: One-Sided, Unrestricted Assignment Right for Veltmar

**Location:** Amendment No. 1, Section 4 (adding new SA Section 14.4), read with Supply Agreement Section 14.3 and Section 15.2.

**What it says:**

- SA Section 14.3 originally barred either party from assigning without the other's prior written consent. This matched Term Sheet Section 8.1.
- New Section 14.4 provides that, "Notwithstanding Section 14.3," Veltmar may assign or transfer the SA, "in whole or in part," "**without the consent of Customer**," to:
  - any Affiliate; or
  - any successor by merger, consolidation, change of control or sale of all or substantially all of the relevant business or assets.
- Notice is due only within 30 days **after** the assignment takes effect.
- Under Section 15.2, the Amendment controls over Section 14.3.

**Why it matters for Harrowgate:**

- **No competitor exclusion.** A Harrowgate competitor, or a company owned by one, could acquire Veltmar or its container business and step into the contract. That company would gain access to Harrowgate's forecasts, volumes, pricing and specifications. Section 12 confidentiality is only a partial protection once the counterparty is a competitor. It would also hold Harrowgate's exclusive supply.
- **No credit, capability or quality protection.**
  - There is no creditworthiness, capability or quality-certification requirement for the assignee.
  - Liability is capped at six months of fees (SA Section 11.1), so Harrowgate's recourse against a thinly capitalized assignee may be limited in practice.
  - The original Veltmar would be released if the assignment is a full transfer, because nothing requires Veltmar to remain liable.
- **Partial assignment.** The "in whole or in part" wording would let Veltmar split the contract, for example assigning certain products or facilities to a lower-quality Affiliate.
- **The restriction is now one-sided.** Harrowgate remains bound by Section 14.3 and cannot assign, even to its own Affiliate or a buyer of its business, without Veltmar's consent. This could become an obstacle in any Harrowgate M&A transaction.
- **The combined effect.** Together with the worldwide exclusivity (Item 3) and the likely five-year renewal (Item 1), Harrowgate could be locked into buying all its containers from an assignee it never approved.

**Information needed from the client:**

1. Is Harrowgate aware of any pending Veltmar sale, restructuring or change of control? (This might explain why Veltmar sought this clause.)
2. Which companies does Harrowgate regard as competitors?
3. Does Harrowgate itself contemplate any restructuring or sale for which mutual assignment flexibility would be valuable?

**Recommended fix:**

Replace Section 14.4 with a mutual provision that adds:

- a competitor exclusion;
- an assignee creditworthiness and capability standard;
- advance notice;
- a guarantee or continuing liability from the assignor; and
- a Harrowgate termination right if a change of control occurs in favor of a competitor.

**Proposed language (replacement Section 14.4):**

> "14.4 **Permitted Assignment.** Notwithstanding Section 14.3, either Party may assign this Agreement in whole, but not in part, without the consent of the other Party, to an Affiliate or to a successor by merger, consolidation, change of control or sale of all or substantially all of the business or assets to which this Agreement relates, provided that (a) the assigning Party gives the other Party at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice; (b) the assignee agrees in writing to be bound by this Agreement; (c) in the case of assignment by Supplier, the assignee has financial standing, production capacity and quality certifications (including those required by the Quality Agreement) at least equivalent to those of Supplier at the date of this Agreement; and (d) the assigning Party remains jointly and severally liable for the assignee's performance. Supplier shall not assign or transfer this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any Competitor of Customer without Customer's prior written consent. If Supplier undergoes a change of control as a result of which a Competitor of Customer controls Supplier, Customer may terminate this Agreement on written notice given within one hundred twenty (120) days after it receives notice of the change of control, without liability other than payment for Products delivered. "**Competitor of Customer**" means any person or entity (or any Affiliate of a person or entity) that bottles, fills or distributes beverage products in competition with Customer or its Affiliates."
